findings.summary: The CODEX-02-A slice is limited to the six authorized source paths plus the controller's results report. It meets all three card acceptance criteria. Anonymous demo anchors need no signup and the page has no identity inputs. Full, paused and unknown states hide the offer and the Join button and promise no delivery. Offer terms come only from a validated, fresh, open synthetic snapshot, and there is no $15/two-game fallback. getDiscoveryView fails closed on missing, extra, invalid, unselected and expired values (including expires_at == now). Join re-checks the snapshot with clock() at click time. Interest is opt-in, starts unchecked and is unsent. Discovery is gated behind isSyntheticPreviewEnabled with the three-flag allowlist kept. Controller evidence (25/25 tests, build, 44 route-identity cases, seeded secret scan) backs this. The remaining gaps are minor evidence and copy issues; the offer, admission, signup (02-B) and consent (10-A) gates stay open.

findings.title: No browser/phone layout or keyboard-focus observation
findings.problem: The card asks for keyboard focus, a phone layout and the forest/paper visual family, and says DOM checks are not phone/browser layout verification. The CSS supplies a :focus-visible outline, 44px targets and a ≤420px column layout, but nobody has observed them in a browser, at phone width or with a keyboard walkthrough. The report says so honestly. This is unverified, not failing.
findings.fix_check: Before any public use, attach an actual phone-width browser observation and a keyboard tab-order walkthrough of /loop-preview/discover, or record it as an open verification item in the acceptance record.

findings.title: Required service-explanation copy has no automated assertion
findings.problem: The card requires visible copy for US geography, ages 5–8, the parent-together role, an AI-generated draft plus mandatory human review, and a 24-hour commitment that starts only at confirmed original production receipt. The component renders all of it (LoopDiscovery.tsx:75-90), but no test asserts it, so a later edit could drop or contradict the copy silently. I could not read the controller checker (permission denied), so I can't confirm the controller covers it either.
findings.fix_check: Add React/jsdom assertions that discovery-family contains the US, ages 5–8, human-review and receipt-start 24-hour text in every fixture state.

findings.title: Report wording is stale against controller evidence
findings.problem: The report mentions 'seven listed output paths' while the instruction lists six. It also describes the tests, build and checker as pending, but the controller has since run them with exit 0. The record should match the final evidence.
findings.fix_check: The acceptance record cites six source paths plus the report, and attaches the controller results (25 pass, build ok, 44 route cases, seeded scan).

findings.title: Offer values are read twice (validate then copy)
findings.problem: Offer fields are checked with nonempty() and then read again to build the copy. An accessor property could return a valid string on the first read and something else on the second. With developer fixtures this has negligible impact, but reading each value once would make the fail-closed guarantee exact.
findings.fix_check: Read each offer key once into a local, validate those values, and return the same values; add a getter-based negative test.
